Photograph: UKRAINIAN PRESIDENTIAL PRESS SERVICE/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Volodymyr Zelenskyy makes a presentation to a Ukrainian soldier during a visit to frontline positions where he named two of Ukraine’s most prominent commanders to spearhead defence of Ukraine’s ‘fortress belt’. Photograph: UKRAINIAN PRESIDENTIAL PRESS SERVICE/AFP/Getty Images Russia-Ukraine war at a glance Ukraine Explainer Ukraine war briefing: Reboot of ‘fortress belt’ defences as Zelenskyy visits frontline Two modern commanders appointed on Donetsk front after dismissal of ‘Soviet-era’ Oleksandr Syrskyi as head of military. What we know on day 1,645 Warren Murray and agencies Wed 26 Aug 2026 21.34 EDT Last modified on Wed 26 Aug 2026 21.35 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Volodymyr Zelenskyy has appointed two of Ukraine’s most prominent commanders to oversee and strengthen defences of the “fortress belt” of industrialised cities in the Donetsk region . Visiting the frontline, Zelenskyy said Third Army Corps leader Andrii Biletskyi and Denys Prokopenko, commander of the First Corps ⁠Azov, would head new groupings. Both units are known for embracing Nato-style doctrine and new technology. Russian forces are putting pressure on the cities of Kostiantynivka, Kramatorsk and Sloviansk – all critical strongholds for Ukraine. According to open-source mapping group Deep State, Moscow’s ‌troops have been infiltrating deeper into Kostiantynivka, with the Ukrainians weeding them out from houses, basements and ruins. Russia was also stepping up its air and artillery ​attacks on Kramatorsk and Sloviansk to prepare for a targeted offensive on those cities, Deep State said. Ukrainian military analyst Mykola Bielieskov told Reuters the appointments were “the right move” in giving Ukraine’s new commander in chief, Mykhailo Drapatyi, greater scope for strategic planning . His predecessor, the “Soviet-era” general Oleksandr Syrskyi, was criticised for micromanagement. Ukrainian drone forces commander Robert Brovdi, a leader of Kyiv’s mid and long-range strike campaigns, praised the appointments as an important step towards “network-centric warfare … This is exactly what ‘Smart War’ is,” he posted. Ukraine hit ⁠16 sites in Russia ⁠over ⁠the past day ​including oil facilities and ⁠logistics , Zelenskyy said ⁠on Wednesday. The ‌targets also included ‌airfields, a missile unit, a military enterprise and infrastructure that ‌Moscow uses to launch attacks against ​Ukraine. Ukraine’s military general staff said its forces struck a Lukoil refinery overnight in Kstovo, in Russia’s Nizhny Novgorod region, setting it on fire. The refinery can process 125m barrels annually. Long-range Ukrainian drones burned a Wildberries warehouse to the ground in the Tambov region south-east of Moscow, Russian authorities said on Wednesday. A ⁠ Russian guided aerial ⁠bomb ⁠attack seriously ​damaged a combined ⁠heat and power plant ⁠in ​ Ukraine’s southern ‌city ‌of Kherson , ‌the plant’s owner, Ukrainian energy company Naftogaz, said ‌on Wednesday. The extent of ​the damage would be ⁠assessed as ​soon as ​the security ​situation allowed, ​Naftogaz ‌said. There were explosions ​in ⁠the ⁠Ukrainian capital ​of ‌Kyiv ‌early ‌on Thursday, ‌a ​Reuters ⁠witness ​said. Around the same time, Russia ⁠attacked an industrial facility ⁠in ⁠the central ​Ukrainian city of ⁠Kryvyi Rih with ballistic missiles, ⁠injuring two ​people, ‌said Oleksandr ‌Vilkul, the head of ‌the city’s defence council. It came after Bloomberg reported that Russia was considering ⁠stepping up its ballistic missile strikes ⁠on ⁠Kyiv , including ​targets in the city centre, ⁠and on critical infrastructure elsewhere in ⁠Ukraine after concluding that ​efforts ‌to negotiate ‌a peace deal ‌had reached a dead end. While Ukraine has repeatedly offered ceasefires and negotiations, the Kremlin has not altered its demands – chief among which is total control of Ukraine’s Donbas region. Volodymyr Zelenskyy has awarded Ukraine’s Order of Freedom to Elon Musk , whose SpaceX has provided Starlink satellite internet to Ukraine’s military. Musk has restricted its use over Russian territory – a policy Zelenskyy hopes to change so that Ukrainian weapons can use Starlink to navigate to their targets. Ukraine freed 10 Russian prisoners of war , Russia’s human rights commissioner said on Wednesday. On Monday, Russia released 10 Ukrainian prisoners of war who were previously thought to be missing. A pro-Russian hacker group on Wednesday claimed responsibility for a cyber-attack on Digdir, the Norwegian government’s digital services agency. The denial-of-service (DDOS) attacks tried to overwhelm the agency’s computers to block services, including one that enables citizens to use one login across multiple public services. A Digdir spokesperson said the agency still managed to keep the services running “practically all the time”. The pro-Russian hacker group Server Killers said it attacked because Norway renewed its security cooperation with Ukraine on 23 August. https://www.nme.com/news/music/watch-cha.text: Chase & Status at the 2026 Leeds Festival at Bramham Park on August 28, 2026 in Leeds, England. (Photo by Matthew Baker/Getty Images) Chase & Status brought Reading 2026 to a close with a star-studded headline set – check out footage below. The UK production duo were the final act on the festival’s main stage – now known as The Grid – at Little John’s Farm last night (August 30), following on from co-headliner Florence + The Machine . Advertisement They were joined by ArrDee for ‘Liquor & Cigarettes’, NADIAH for ‘Count On Me’, D Double E for ‘Levels’ and Novelist for ‘NRG’ in the first half of their set, which took place against a torrential downpour for the Reading crowd. IRAH contributed vocals during a mash-up of the duo’s remixes of Britney Spears ‘ ‘Toxic’ and Shy FX and UK Apache’s ‘Original Nuttah’, while Flowdan came out for ‘Baddadan’ and Takura joined for ‘No Problem’. WATCH Tom Grennan made an appearance on ‘All Goes Wrong’, Clementine Douglas was there for ‘Mixed Emotions’, Debbie sang on ‘Gone Too Far’, and Liam Bailey came out for the band’s classic single ‘Blind Faith’. “If you’ve been with us since the beginning…old and new fans, we appreciate the fuck out of you. Reading, make some fucking noise for yourselves,” the duo said as the show came to an end. UK viewers can watch the full set here . Chase & Status’ Reading 2026 setlist was: ‘Rage’ ‘Selecta’ ‘Streetlife’ ‘Disgruntled’ ‘Liquor & Cigarettes’ (with ArrDee) ‘Count On Me’ (with NADIAH) ‘Levels’ (with D Double E) ‘Don’t Be Scared’ ‘NRG’ (with Novelist) ‘Toxic (Chase & Status Remix)’ / ‘Original Nuttah 25 (Chase & Status Remix)’ (with IRAH) ‘Baddadan’ (with Flowdan) ‘Disconnect’ ‘No Problem’ (with Takura) ‘Backbone’ ‘Mixed Emotions’ (with Clementine Douglas) ‘Gone Too Far’ (with Debbie) ‘All Goes Wrong’ (with Tom Grennan) ‘Carnage’ ‘Blind Faith’ (with Liam Bailey) ‘Program’ (with IRAH) Recommended Earlier this month, the duo joined Skrillex during his own headline set at Boomtown for a surprise B2B performance. They played an unreleased track with Brazilian vocals, with many fans speculating that it points to an upcoming collaboration between the two. They also performed at Romania’s Electric Castle festival in July, where their rendition of ‘Baddadan’ sparked “pandemonium among hordes of skanking teens” . The duo are currently preparing to release their eighth studio album, ‘Generic Everything’, on October 9. The record includes Reading setlist tracks ‘Disgruntled’, ‘Levels’, ‘Gone Too Far’ and ‘Carnage’. https://www.politico.eu/article/palantir.text: LONDON — The Mayor of London Sadiq Khan and U.S. tech company Palantir have agreed to drop legal proceedings relating to a blocked £50 million police contract. Palantir brought a claim against the Mayor’s Office for Policing and Crime in the High Court in June after Khan’s deputy mayor refused to sign off on the £50 million contract with the Metropolitan Police for the provision of an AI and data analysis service. In July, lawyers working on behalf of MOPAC in turn accused the Met Police and Palantir of coordinating to fix the outcome of the procurement process in breach of the rules . Palantir claimed Khan’s office had unlawfully blocked the contract over the company's “values and ethics,” based on media reporting. Advertisement Advertisement A full trial was expected in January but on Wednesday both sides agreed to “settle their differences” and drop the allegations without admitting liability. They will each cover their own legal costs. In an agreed statement , the two sides said MOPAC’s decision to block the Palantir contract was “not based on Palantir’s values or ethics or any wider reporting about the company,” though MOPAC said it “recognizes Palantir’s concerns that media reporting of a statement from the Mayor's spokesperson before the decision was taken could have incorrectly created the impression that an assessment of the company’s values had been a factor in that decision.” “MOPAC’s consideration was based upon its statutory role of examining spend proposals, against the appropriate legal tests and the relevant guidance on procurement, governance, affordability and ensuring value for money for Londoners and in doing so it focussed on the available information at the time,” the statement said. The settlement also notes that MOPAC is working with Metropolitan Police Service to re-run a competitive procurement for the relevant service, which Palantir will be eligible to bid for. “MOPAC does not have, and has never had, any policy of not contracting with Palantir,” the statement confirms, while noting the mayor’s duty is to ensure “all procurements are lawful, fair, transparent and deliver value for money.” “London is the technology capital of Europe, and I am proud that leading software firms choose the city as their home. Palantir makes a significant contribution to jobs and investment in the capital, employing a large number of Londoners whose services have been procured legally by organizations across the U.K. and beyond,” Khan said. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/videos/c65yng.text: Why Zelensky's meeting with Burnham matters Why Zelensky's meeting with Burnham matters Close Prime Minister Andy Burnham welcomed President Volodymyr Zelensky to Downing Street on Wednesday, as the Ukrainian leader looks to shore up his European allies five years into Russia's war on Ukraine. Burnham told Zelensky that Britain "would forever stand by you" and that he was accelerating the delivery of air defences to Ukraine. Burnham previously told MPs that he would try to "repair bridges" between Ukraine and the United States and that Ukraine won't leave "empty-handed". The two leaders met at No 10 Downing Street where Zelensky was welcomed with a military ceremonial guard - thought to be a first for a foreign leader. BBC World News correspondent Joe Inwood explains what we know about the meeting. Read more about the meeting in London. https://www.dw.com/en/italy-students-and.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OrcS Prefer DW on Google Students demanding education and housing support joined workers protesting rising living costs and military spending across Italy Image: Andreas Solaro/AFP Advertisement Tens of thousands of students and workers marched across Italy on Friday, demanding more education funding and relief from rising living costs. The rallies followed weeks of student tent camps and school occupations, with a general strike bringing workers into the streets alongside them. Demonstrations took place in dozens of cities, including Rome, Milan, Turin, Bologna, Genoa and Naples. Police were deployed in large numbers after earlier protests descended into rioting. Why were students and workers protesting? Demonstrators criticized Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni 's right-wing government over low wages, rising fuel prices and military spending. Students demanded more money for schools and universities. In Rome, university student Beatrice Chilelli said students were "at a breaking point." "They can't afford to pay exorbitant tuition fees, and rent... which weighs heavily on their parents' shoulders," the 21-year-old told AFP. Like their French counterparts, students in Italy have been protesting for weeks Image: Marco Bertorello/AFP The USB trade union called a general strike, with truck drivers, taxi drivers and farmers among those joining the protests. Disruption to public transport remained limited on Friday morning. Thousands marched from Rome's Termini station past the Colosseum, accompanied by two tractors and a taxi. "We need more houses, not bombs!" one group chanted. Did the protests turn violent? Minor scuffles broke out between demonstrators and riot police in Turin at the start of the march. No major clashes had been reported by midday. In Milan, the procession headed away from the city center, where rioters looted shops, damaged property and clashed with police after a cost-of-living demonstration two weeks earlier. Authorities also increased protection around landmarks, including Rome's Colosseum and Milan's cathedral. The student protests have drawn momentum from similar movements in France and Spain . Teachers, retirees and other workers also joined Friday's rallies. https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/p.text: Explore the ABC Poland treats fatal mass shooting as 'terrorist offence' amid two days of mourning Topic: Unrest, Conflict and War Posted Mon 9 Nov 2026 at 7:25am Mon 9 Nov 2026 at 7:25am Mon 9 Nov 2026 at 7:25am Loading... In short: Polish prosecutors say a mass shooting that killed six people and injured at least 15 is being treated as an act "constituting a terrorist offence". The square where the shooting occurred has reopened, with mourners gathering to lay flowers and candles. What's next? Poland has entered two days of national mourning. abc.net.au/news/poland-treating-mass-shooting-as-terrorist-offence/107362106 Link copied Share Share article Polish prosecutors say a mass shooting that killed six people and injured at least 15 others is being treated as an act "constituting a terrorist offence". The attack, which Poland's defence minister described as an "act of terror," happened on Saturday, local time, in the Main Square in the heart of Krakow's Old Town. The square is a major tourist hub in the country's second-largest city. Polish police guarded Krakow's Main Square more than a day after the shooting. ( Reuters: Jakub Porzyck ) Four women and two men were killed in the shooting . Three of the women and one of the men were Polish, according to Malopolska regional governor Krzysztof Jan Klęczar. A man from the United Kingdom and a woman from Austria were also among the dead, authorities said. A video posted on social media showed a police officer repeatedly shooting the attacker, who was lying on the street. The officer later slowly collapsed to the ground. Poland has entered two days of national mourning. ( Reuters: Jakub Porzycki ) The two police officers who stopped the gunman, in actions authorities hailed as heroic, remain in hospital. They were both conscious by Sunday afternoon. The bodies of the assailant's sister, mother and father were also found at the man's family home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, a city about 150 kilometres north-east of Krakow. They likely died from gunshot wounds. The square reopened on Sunday evening, with mourners gathering to lay flowers and candles in honour of the victims. Poland has entered two days of national mourning. St. Mary's Trumpet Call, a traditional five-note melody which played every hour from the highest tower of St Mary's Basilica, was paused overnight — the first time the call had been missed since World War II. Witnesses recall moments of chaos Marie-Ange Collaer wrote on Facebook that she and her family survived the shooting during a trip to Krakow from Brussels. "We literally ran for our lives and managed to hide from the bullets flying around," she wrote. " Lying on the floor in a shop like in a bad police movie whilst you hear bullets everywhere. " British resident Neil Thaxton and his wife also lived through the attack. "We had just walked through the main square and heard the gunshots," he wrote on Facebook. "We thought it was fireworks then people started running, we went into a gift shop and the staff took us in the back of the shop and locked the doors and turned the lights off." Witnesses who survived the shooting say they scrambled to find refuge in nearby stores. ( Reuters: Jakub Porzycki ) Alexandros Maronitis, a tourist from Greece, told The Associated Press that he could not get back to his lodgings for five hours after the shooting. "We saw the shooter when they picked him up with the ambulance," he said. "So, we're a bit afraid. It's our first time in Poland. We heard it's a safe country." Krakow's St Anne's Church was packed with people who attended a memorial service. ( AP: Jakub Porzycki ) Witness Andy Hill told the BBC he felt as though he was in a movie scene. "It doesn't feel real," he said. "And the trouble is, you have such an instantaneous moment to make a decision: Run. Stand still. There's an element of shock. But I just thought the easiest thing to do is dive through a doorway and just take refuge behind the windows." Grim first for Poland Poland's Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said the suspect held "very radical" and "ultranationalistic" views. "Everything indicates that he was fascinated by far-right ideologies," he said at a news conference on Saturday. At least six killed in shooting in Krakow Four women and two men are dead, 15 others are injured and the gunman is in hospital after a shooting in a market square in the Polish city of Krakow. Local officials in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski said they seized seven weapons from the family home, bringing the total number recovered to 11, including four found on the suspect or in his car in Krakow. Both father and son had gun permits, they said. The suspect, a Polish citizen, remains in a critical condition after undergoing multiple surgeries. There was confusion on Saturday about his age, with authorities first saying 24 and later 25. On Sunday they confirmed he was 24. The suspect's dead sibling was a young artist studying at the Krakow Academy of Fine Arts. "Nothing will ever be like before. The delicate tissue of our academic community was painfully wounded," the academy wrote in a statement on Sunday. A shooting club in Starachowice, where the suspect is believed to have trained, said it only offered "static shooting". ( Reuters: Kacper Pempel ) The academy confirmed Magdalena Oksińska was a third year student and that, additionally, the sister of an academy employee was shot twice. "Magdalena Oksińska, 21 years old, a queer person, was an absolutely talented painter, photographer, poet and writer," architect Pavko Krajka wrote in a post on social media, accompanied by images of the artist's colourful paintings. About 411,000 people hold gun permits in Poland, which has a population of 37 million, and interest in gun ownership has been rising. The Swit shooting club in Starachowice, where the suspect is believed to have trained, issued a statement on Sunday saying it offered only "static shooting," which involves firing from a fixed position at a stationary target. The club said the suspect "was never trained in our club in the areas of dynamic, tactical or combat shooting". Mass shootings are uncommon in Poland, however, in mid-October three attacks at schools in the central province of Mazovia took place within four days, leaving one person dead and many injured, including children. The Krakow shooter's military gear, guns and overall look were similar to those of other "extreme right lone actors" committing attacks around Europe, said Kacper Rekawek, a senior researcher at the International Center for Counterterrorism in The Hague. "We have had attempts before, but now we can say that these kinds of attacks have become successful in Poland," he said. Make us your Google favorite Exports of Greek oranges are still proceeding at a rather slow pace. According to official data from the Directorate of Quality and Food Safety of the Greek Ministry of Rural Development and Food, exports up to November 6 amounted to just 3,680 tonnes, whereas by the same date last year, they had already exceeded twice that volume. Giorgos Ntokos, president of the packer-exporter Helmi King Fruit, based in Argolida, comments on the market situation: "There is some demand, but it is not particularly strong yet. November has not gone as well as we would have liked. We have fulfilled the initial orders, but we will probably have to wait until the end of the month for both the market and Greek supply to pick up." © Helmi King Fruit As Ntokos explains, Greek packers are currently finding it particularly difficult to source Navelinas larger than No. 5. "In Argolida, one of the main growing regions for Navelinas, production is considerably higher compared with last season, but most of the fruit falls into size No. 5. Growers do not have the financial means to manage their orchards properly. Now, Navelinas will not grow any larger, but they still need to undergo technical degreening, which adds to the cost. This process will certainly have to continue until mid-December. For the time being, we prefer to focus on harvesting oranges from orchards at higher elevations, as they have higher Brix levels," Ntokos states. "The shortage of larger fruit makes it difficult to serve one of our main markets, Poland. Some markets are more receptive to smaller fruit, but whenever we need to meet demand for sizes larger than No. 5, we really find it very difficult. For the moment we struggle to find oranges in sizes 1, 2 and 3. What else can we do? We cannot pump them up." Indeed, according to official data, Greek orange exports to Poland are currently close to zero. However, the situation may improve in a few weeks. "Things in Argolida will improve once the Merlin variety is ready.
